meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'egg' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Берём свежие яйца и разогреваем сковороду.
examples.trans: We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-парижски').

examples.text: На завтрак мы приготовили нежное яйцо по-парижски.
examples.trans: For breakfast we prepared a delicate Parisian-style egg.

examples.text: Весь интерьер нашего зала оформлен изысканно и по-парижски.
examples.trans: The entire interior of our dining room is decorated elegantly in Parisian style.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to expect') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

снять.gloss: to film, to photograph; to take off; to rent

meanings.en: to film, to take a photo/video of
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to film', forming an aspectual pair with 'снимать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to take off, to remove') (clothing) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('to rent') (a flat or room) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон.
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone.
He took off his coat by the door.

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон. И сразу все мне помогают!
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone. And right away everyone helps me!

meanings.note: кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом
Secondary conversational sense ('to name') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'понсор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sponsor, backer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы не можем продолжать кампанию без спонсоров.
examples.trans: We cannot continue the campaign without sponsors.

examples.text: Мы не можем продолжать кампанию без спонсоров. Нам даже плакаты напечатать не на что.
examples.trans: We cannot continue the campaign without sponsors. We don't even have money to print posters.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: pointing at something a little way off
Secondary conversational sense ('out!') (вон отсюда! = get out of here!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'from here'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'matter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('matter, business') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('case (in court)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'full house' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Завтра вечером в ресторане будет полный аншлаг.
examples.trans: Tomorrow evening there will be a full house at the restaurant.

examples.text: По субботам у нас всегда настоящий аншлаг.
examples.trans: On Saturdays we always have a real full house.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('even') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Everyday conversational Russian name meaning 'Bianca', frequent in spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arrive (by vehicle)', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'trump card' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня есть еще один козырь.
examples.trans: I have another ace up my sleeve.

examples.text: У меня в запасе есть ещё один сильный козырь.
examples.trans: I have one more strong trump card in reserve.

examples.text: Фирменный соус шефа — это главный козырь нашего меню.
examples.trans: The chef's signature sauce is the main trump card of our menu.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'бронировать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to reserve', forming an aspectual pair with 'бронировать'.

examples.text: Макс решил забронировать столик на вечер.
examples.trans: Max decided to reserve a table for the evening.

examples.text: Алло, ресторан, я хочу забронировать столик.
examples.trans: Hello, restaurant, I want to reserve a table.
Book a table for Prokhor Mikhailov.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'small table'.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian name meaning 'Prokhor', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Book a table for Prokhor Mikhailov.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian name meaning 'Mikhailova', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Book a table for Prokhor Mikhailov.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'oligarch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The oligarch will dine with us?

examples.text: Знаменитый олигарх будет сегодня ужинать в нашем ресторане?
examples.trans: Will the famous oligarch be dining at our restaurant tonight?

examples.text: Для стола олигарха заказали самую дорогую чёрную икру.
examples.trans: The most expensive black caviar was ordered for the oligarch's table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to dine'.

examples.trans: The oligarch will dine with us?

examples.text: Знаменитый олигарх будет сегодня вечером ужинать у нас?
examples.trans: Will the famous oligarch be dining at our place tonight?

examples.text: После смены мы иногда остаёмся вместе тихо ужинать в зале.
examples.trans: After the shift we sometimes stay to quietly have dinner together in the hall.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Secondary conversational sense ('exactly, precisely') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable feminine noun meaning 'meeting', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('see you') (in 'до встречи' = until we meet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?
